claims.text: The component material is susceptible to hot cracking when subjected to fusion welding.
Friction stir welding can repair the damaged region without melting the base material.
Friction stir welding uses friction-generated heat and severe plastic deformation to join material in the solid state.
Friction stir welding avoids temperatures that cause melting.
Avoiding melting eliminates the conditions that promote hot cracking.
Mechanical mixing and dynamic recrystallization during friction stir welding refine the stir-zone grain structure.
Mechanical mixing during friction stir welding homogenizes the stir-zone microstructure.
The refined and homogenized stir-zone structure avoids formation of brittle phases associated with hot cracking.
Mechanical mixing and dynamic recrystallization improve weld-zone microstructural integrity relative to a fusion weld.
Traditional fusion-welding repair necessarily involves melting and subsequent solidification.
Melting and solidification in traditional fusion-welding repair produce regions vulnerable to hot cracking.
Traditional fusion-welding repair produces reduced mechanical performance in this material.
The friction-stir-welded repair will be crack-free and superior to a traditional fusion-welded repair.
The friction-stir-welded area will have enhanced mechanical performance relative to a traditional fusion-welded repair.
The friction-stir-welded area will have greater resistance to hot cracking than a traditional fusion-welded repair.
The friction-stir-welded repair will sustain aggressive operating conditions without premature failure.
Residual stresses introduced during repair may cause unexpected degradation during long-term cyclic loading.
